newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee erases losses, eyes on stock data.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee erases losses, eyes on stock data.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures regained some strength in the afternoon to end steady to higher, boosted by trade buying after early Far East origin selling dried up.
Traders said business was routine and prices remained in a range. All eyes were, however, focused on key U.S. stock data due after the close of trading on Friday.
By the close, benchmark January stood at $1,430 a tonne, the same as Wednesday's finish, after hitting a session low of $1,416 and just above a key support of $1,415.
Volume was 2,642 lots, dominated by the January position. Traders noted active Jan/March switches traded at a wide range of between $52 and $58 at a few times.
At the clsoe, the spread narrowed to $52 from the last finish of $62.
Immediately, traders are awaiting two key supply data due on Friday to help set direction.
LIFFE's October certified coffee stocks are due at around 1230 GMT Friday. Traders expect the data to show a slight rise in view of the recent strong November premium to the back months.
But the more closely-watched is the monthly inventory data from the Green Coffee Association of New York, due after the close on Friday.
Most traders expected the report to show a decline of between 200,000 and 300,000 60-kg bags, although one trader predicted the drawdown could be as large as 500,000 bags.
"There's an expectation that it will be down quite significantly and I think's that's helping the market, New York-wise," said one London trader.

In physical news, Thursday marked the start of Ivory Coast's 1996/97 coffee marketing campaign with the farm-gate price slashed to 500 CFA francs per kg of green bagged coffee to reflect a slump in world prices.
The previous recommended price was 700 CFA. Both prices include five CFA for the sack.
Elsewhere, the U.S. Department of Agriculture has revised estimates for Colombia green coffee production in the current and the next marketing year due to unfavourable weather.

The USDA pegged 1995/96 output at 12 million 60-kg bags, down from 12.5 million. It also lowered forecast for the 1996/97 campaign to 12.5 million from 13 million. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
